chosen:
I chose "decisive": design r. It relays the learner's own inner-discovery record across categories through the kernel's existing memory channel. The relay is decided once, on the four fresh categories, by one primary test that is replicated over chains and controlled on three fronts: on-policy against off-policy, against a placebo, and against equal compute.

Kept from that proposal:
- where the recursion sits: it learns from the dense variant outcomes inside acquisition, at training budget 200;
- the frozen, off-policy, shuffled, o0@matched and frozen@4B arms;
- one primary endpoint at alpha 0.01, a fixed-sequence and Holm gate, and a non-binding futility look;
- the diagnostics that name the limit of a negative result, and the alpha-spending rule across attempts.

Changed:
1. 64 chains x 2 seeds instead of 32 x 4. This uses the same number of held-out runs but tolerates the unmeasured chain variance: MDE80 is 0.0054-0.0074 instead of 0.0064-0.0098.
2. A new credit rule: probability matching on the positive margin d+, with exact ties excluded. It replaces mean d shrunk toward 0, which would favour no-op cells such as pick edits on ordered job shop.
3. The placebo is a uniform random permutation of the cell labels, drawn per chain. The old derangement was anti-informative.
4. A runtime dispatch in a new file replaces the edit to designs.py, which registration_o pins and whose later stages check its hash.
5. Two grafted channels:
   - a library of program blocks taken from kept inner switches, inserted again by a splice edit with its constants relocated (reusable primitives that change across generations);
   - a prior over edit sizes, so the size of exploratory moves is learned from the record.
6. Matching partially mutable controls: library-only (retained macros, the Owner's comparison 3) and prior-only.
7. m_net is defined, a retention endpoint is added, and the figures the judges flagged are corrected.
grafted: From level: the library L0 of program blocks that stay live in kept programs, inserted again by a splice edit. Here the blocks come from confirmed inner switches, constants added by a block are relocated to new constants, and a term block is appended at the end of the program. Also from level: a skills-only control, here library-only (retained macros with no learned operator selection), standing for the Owner's comparison 3, and the argument that identical untrained answers make min(change of acquired, change of gain) equal to the change of acquired.

From generator: disjoint seeds per replicate (per chain here), so no common parent-seed offset enters every measurement. Predictions are recorded before the outcomes (L6 is prospective: the prior is fixed before any held-out run and is checked against off-policy per-cell outcomes in the frozen runs). Candidate size is learned from the record (the edit-size prior, the inner analogue of macro-edits). Planted-effect tests of the estimator.

From statistics: replication at the chain level with more chains, so the design tolerates the unmeasured between-replicate variance (64 x 2 instead of 32 x 4 at equal held-out cost). Also: a per-generation transfer measurement (L7, at the positions where the chain switches category); a rho-hat analogue (L4, the cross-category correlation of the learned per-cell statistics); a non-binding futility look; the machine-time factor of 1.15, because run.py scores the training instances after its CPU fields.

From unconventional: a registered arm priority list under a CPU cap, fixed from instance sizes before any held-out run, so that a binding cap drops only secondary arms. A replay-equivalence test (empty memory gives design q bit for bit). Development go/no-go gates that record the negative result and stop. The shuffled arm doubles as an empirical placebo.

From the judges: a uniform random permutation as the placebo instead of a derangement; tau measured in development and used by a pre-written (J, S) rule; m_net defined; a retention endpoint; corrected figures. Five times the budget buys o0 +0.0053, not +0.006. Design o's false acceptance is 0.0083-0.0103 per step in the worst case; multiplied by the measured confirmation share of 4/29 it is 0.011-0.014 per 10-step lineage. budget_scaling's 0.015 to 0.006 is the noise of edit-minus-parent means over eight edits (heteroscedastic; job shop's sigma rose from 0.0068 to 0.0197), not o0's noise and not evidence of more precision per CPU-second.
spec:
DESIGN R: THE LEARNER'S OWN DISCOVERY RECORD, RELAYED ACROSS CATEGORIES (OPERATOR PRIOR, EDIT-SIZE PRIOR, BLOCK LIBRARY), DECIDED ONCE ON FOUR UNSEEN CATEGORIES

0. FILES AND SCHEDULE

0.1 New files only (about 1,300 lines):
- rsi6/learner/design_r.py (~330 lines)
- rsi6/learner/dispatch_r.py (~50 lines)
- rsi6/open/relay.py (~400 lines)
- rsi6/open/relay_report.py (~280 lines)
- rsi6/tests/test_design_r.py (~240 lines)
- rsi6/registry/registration_r.json
- rsi6/registry/amendment_6.json (the next free amendment number; 6 unless taken).

0.2 Unchanged files, pinned by sha256 in registration_r.files:
- kernel: rsi6/kernel/run.py, problem.py, environment.py, ledger.py, roles.py (so the meter and the references are unchanged);
- learner: rsi6/learner/designs.py, design_o.py, design_q.py, design_b.py, learner.py, version.py;
- open: rsi6/open/edits.py, evaluate.py;
- experiments: rsi6/experiments/report.py, guard.py;
- environments: rsi6/environments/__init__.py, plus the adapters and manifests of jobshop, quadassign, pmedian, knapsack, binpacking and of the four fresh categories;
- rsi6/registry/roles.json.
designs.py keeps the hash that registration_o pins (7d47aa5b...).

0.3 Ledgers and CPU:
- Registered stages write ledger/live.jsonl through guard.single_writer. They therefore run only when no stage of registration_o is running.
- Development writes scratch ledgers rsi6/ledger/dev_r_<check>.jsonl. It refuses any category whose effective role is not source. It waits while ledger/.writer.lock is held, so the running experiment's CPU-seconds are not perturbed.
- OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1; the kernel's 4 workers.

1. dispatch_r.py

install() is idempotent. It saves designs._module, designs.make and designs.default, then replaces them:
- _module(v): design_q if designs.design_of(v) == 'q', design_r if 'r', else the saved _module(v);
- make(v): design_q.LearnerQ(v), design_r.LearnerR(v), else the saved make(v);
- default(d): design_q.default() or design_r.default(), else the saved default(d).

Why this works without editing designs.py:
- designs.digest, validate, differences and schema look up the global _module at call time, so they follow the replacement.
- kernel/run.py looks up designs.make and designs.digest at call time and forks its multiprocessing pool after install(). Runs of designs q and r therefore pass through the unchanged kernel.
- For designs a, b and o, every call reaches the original function object.

relay.py, relay_report.py and the tests call install() before anything else.

2. design_r.py

2.1 Constants
- BASE_CELLS = design_q.INNER_CELLS: 18 cells in design_q's order. They are, for score and for pick: insert, delete, replace, mutop, mutarg, swap, term, cross; then theta/perturb and theta/grow.
- SPLICE_CELLS = [('score','splice'), ('pick','splice')].
- CELLS = BASE_CELLS + SPLICE_CELLS: 20 cells. Every per-cell array is indexed by CELLS.
- BASE_THETA = 10.
- PARAMLIKE = ('scale', 'shift', 'const'): the score and pick ops whose field b is a theta index.
- KIND_STATS = 'r_stats'; KIND_LIB = 'r_lib'; ENTRY_V = 1.
- RELAY0 = {beta 1.0, kappa 20.0, cap 2.0, lib_max 32, lib_per_run 4, rule 'dplus'}.

2.2 Version
A design-q record with design 'r' and one more part, 'relay'.
- default(): design_q.default() with design 'r' and relay = RELAY0, changed only by D2's pre-written rules.
- validate(v):
  - key set exactly design_q.O_KEYS + {inner, relay}, design 'r';
  - the q-part (v without relay, with design 'q') goes through design_q.validate;
  - relay fields: beta in [0.1, 4]; kappa in [1, 1000]; cap in (0, 8]; lib_max an integer in [0, 64]; lib_per_run an integer in [0, 8]; rule in {dplus, dmean};
  - floats rounded to 6 places.
- digest: sha256 of the canonical JSON of validate(v).
- differences: design_q.differences of the q-parts, plus each changed relay field.
- SCHEMA = {}.
- make(v) = LearnerR(v).
r0 = default() is the only version used by any r arm.

2.3 prior_from(entries, relay): a pure function
1. stats = the entries with kind r_stats and v 1. blocks = the blocks of the entries with kind r_lib and v 1, in order. If neither exists, return None.
2. Sum the 20-element arrays N, U, S, Q and the 3-element arrays NE, UE, SE, QE over stats. n = sum(N).
3. Rule dplus. If n >= 1 and sum(U) > 0:
   - ubar = sum(U)/n
   - m_c = (U_c + kappa*ubar)/(N_c + kappa)
   - w_c = clip(beta*ln(m_c/ubar), -cap, cap)
   - mE_k = (UE_k + kappa*ubar)/(NE_k + kappa)
   - wE_k = clip(beta*ln(mE_k/ubar), -cap, cap)
   Otherwise w = wE = 0.
4. Rule dmean (pre-written alternative):
   - dbar = sum(S)/n
   - s = sqrt(max(sum(Q)/n - dbar^2, 1e-6))
   - m_c = (S_c + kappa*dbar)/(N_c + kappa)
   - w_c = clip(beta*(m_c - dbar)/s, -cap, cap); the same for edit sizes.
5. library = the blocks made unique by canonical JSON, keeping the last occurrence; then the last lib_max of them.
6. Return {w[20], wE[3], library, n, entries}, floats rounded to 6 places.

2.4 Credit, accumulated per acquisition
In each program round, take the i-th non-None variant (aligned with cands[1:]):
- k = the number of edits applied (1 to 3), with cells c_1..c_k;
- d = (F[i] - F[0])/(len(cands) - 1), where F = design_o._fitness(keys) on the round's batch;
- the variant is tied if keys[i] == keys[0] on every batch problem, in both components.

Tied variants count only in 'variants'. Each informative variant adds:
- for each of its cells: N += 1/k, U += max(d,0)/k, S += d/k, Q += d^2/k, W += [d > 0]/k;
- NE[k-1] += 1, UE[k-1] += max(d,0), SE[k-1] += d, QE[k-1] += d^2.
A confirmed switch adds SW += 1/k to each of its cells.

2.5 class LearnerR(design_q.LearnerQ)

__init__(version):
  full = validate(version); super().__init__(the q-part of full); self.relay = full['relay']; self._prior = None.

acquire(problems, rng, memory=None):
1. entries = list((memory or {}).get('entries', [])).
2. Prediction form: the design-o path; return memory {'entries': entries}.
3. Assignment form:
   - self._prior = prior_from(entries, self.relay); reset the log;
   - capability, report = self._acquire_open(problems, rng);
   - new = self._new_entries(capability, problems[0]);
   - report['relay'] = {prior: None or {w and wE rounded to 4 places, library size, n, entries}, new_entries: new};
   - return capability, {'entries': entries + new}, report.
Entries of other kinds pass through untouched and are never read. apply is inherited from design q: a capability that carries programs is answered with them.

_variant(prog, theta, rng):
- With self._prior None, it makes exactly the random draws of design_q.LearnerQ._variant:
  - cells = BASE_CELLS; p = design_q.softmax(inner.w); ed = inner.edits;
  - n = 1 + rng.choice(3, p = ed/sum(ed));
  - for each edit, up to 12 tries of rng.choice(len(cells), p = p), then edits.apply_edit(g, cell, [], rng), with design q's random start for an added constant.
  It also records the cells applied and the edit infos.
- With a prior:
  - cells = BASE_CELLS plus each splice cell whose part has at least one library block;
  - logits = inner.w for the base cells and 0 for splice cells, plus the prior's w for those cells;
  - p = design_q.softmax(logits); ed proportional to inner.edits * exp(wE);
  - a splice cell calls splice().
- It returns what design q's _variant returns, and appends {cells, k, infos} (or None) to self._vlog.

splice(g, part, library, rng):
1. Take the library blocks of that part; if there are none, return (None, 'no block').
2. blk = blocks[rng.integers(len(blocks))]; n0 = len(g['theta']).
3. Refuse if n0 + blk.fresh > 32, or if the program would exceed design_o.LIMITS[part].
4. Append fresh new constants to theta, each round(clip(rng.normal(0,1), -50, 50), 6).
5. In PARAMLIKE instructions, every b < 0 becomes n0 + (-1 - b).
6. Position: the end of the program if blk.term, else rng.integers(len(prog) + 1).
7. design_o.validate; if invalid, return (None, reason).
8. info = {part, kind 'splice', block: the inserted instructions}.

_acquire_open:
A copy of design_q.LearnerQ._acquire_open at its registered hash, with three insertions and nothing else changed:
- self._vlog = [] before a program round's variants;
- the credit of 2.4 after that round's F;
- on a confirmed switch, the switched variant's log entry appended to self._switches.
The report key design becomes 'r'.

_new_entries(capability, P0):
(a) A stats entry:
   - kind 'r_stats', v 1;
   - N, U, S, Q, W, SW: 20 values each, rounded to 6 places;
   - NE, UE, SE, QE: 3 values each;
   - rounds, variants, informative, switches;
   - kept = ('program' in capability), kept_splice;
   - layout {ordered, binary (n_opts == 2), capacity (capacity is not None)}.
(b) A library entry, only when the capability keeps programs:
   - go from the last switch to the first;
   - take each edit info that has a block, whose part (info['target'] or info['part']) is score or pick, and whose every instruction is in design_o.live(the kept program of that part);
   - relocate: in PARAMLIKE instructions, each b >= BASE_THETA becomes -1 - j, in order of first appearance; fresh = the number of such constants; term = the last instruction is ['add', 0, 0, r] with r != 0;
   - keep the first lib_per_run unique blocks, as {kind 'r_lib', v 1, blocks}; omit the entry when there are none.

Invariants, all tested:
- with no r_stats and no r_lib entry, design r is generation 0 of design q (same capability, answers and report counts);
- the memory never holds a fresh-instance score, an answer or a reference;
- nothing beyond design q's unmetered compilation is spent outside the meter.

3. INNER STEP AND ITS ACCEPTANCE RULE (design q's, unchanged)
Rounds alternate at share 0.5. A parameter round is design o's learning-principle round. A program round runs as follows:
1. rng_order draws batch B1 and confirming batch B2, each of 4 fit problems.
2. _variant makes 8 variants of (the current programs, the principle's state A[0]).
3. The incumbent and the variants construct on B1; F is computed; credit is assigned.
4. best = argmax F. If best > 0 and F[best] > F[0], the incumbent and the best variant construct on B2.
5. The learner switches if and only if F2[1] > F2[0]. On a switch, the principle restarts around the new constants.
At the end, the held-back check compares start, state and last_best; a learned option must beat start strictly. The switch rule makes no claim. Its noise is measured (L3), not controlled.

4. THE RECURSION
One generation step is one acquisition of a chain. Position k of chain j acquires category ORDER[k] with memory M_j^(k), and then M_j^(k+1) = M_j^(k) + the new_entries of that run's report.

What position k discovered sets three things in position k+1's representation search:
- the distribution over the 20 cells, from which cells produced variants that beat the incumbent and by how much;
- the distribution over edit sizes;
- the splice library, from the blocks of kept switches.

The chain is on-policy: the variants each update learns from were drawn by the distribution that the earlier updates produced. Evaluation and the claim's acceptance rule are fixed.

5. MEMORY TRANSFORMS (pure functions in relay.py, all tested)
- M_j = M_j^(12). M'_j = the new_entries of off-policy chain j's 12 runs, each run with memory None, concatenated in position order.
- Arms:
  - relay: M_j
  - frozen: None
  - prioronly: M_j without r_lib entries
  - libonly: M_j without r_stats entries
  - depth k: M_j^(k), for k in {4, 8}
  - offpolicy: M'_j
- shuffled:
  - pi_j = default_rng([29, crc32(b'shuffle'), j]).permutation(20), and sigma_j = the same generator's permutation(3);
  - every 20-array a of every r_stats entry becomes a'[c] = a[pi_j[c]], and every 3-array becomes b'[k] = b[sigma_j[k]];
  - every library block is replaced, using rng2 = default_rng([29, crc32(b'shuffle-lib'), j]), by a random block with the same part, length, fresh count and term flag;
  - a term block keeps the skeleton: load r s a, [load r2 s2 a2, mul r r r2], norm r r 0 (norm one of mm, rank, z), scale r r -1, add 0 0 r. Here r, s, a and norm are redrawn, using quiet sensors only;
  - any other block gets edits.random_instruction(part, 10, rng2) for each instruction.
- A job's memory is None for an empty list, else {'entries': list}.

6. DRIVER relay.py
CLI: python -m rsi6.open.relay --stage meta|heldout [--ledger PATH] [--dev d1|d2|d4|dry]

Start-up:
- dispatch_r.install().
- guard checks as in experiment_q: a registered run if and only if the ledger is ledger/live.jsonl; development if and only if the ledger is a scratch ledger; same_history; single_writer.
- File hashes against registration_r.files, and designs.digest(design_r.default()) == generation_0.version_digest.
- On the first registered start: guard.amendment(ledger, 6, what), then a {type 'registration_r', digest, registration} record. Later starts require the same digest.
- Records go through discovery.append_once, so a restarted stage replays and checks itself.

Budgets:
- META = {train 200.0, test_c 2.0, test_e 1.0, n_train 16, n_fresh 24, part 'A'}
- RETAIN = META with part 'B'
- HELD(c) = {train T_c, test_c 2.0, test_e 1.0, n_train 16, n_fresh 24}
- CEIL(c) = HELD(c) with train 4*T_c
- REF = evaluate.RUN_BUDGET

6.1 Stage meta
All five categories must have effective role source.
- ORDER = [jobshop x3, quadassign x3, pmedian x3, knapsack x2, binpacking x1], positions 0 to 11.
- On-policy chains: j < J, with J = 64 unless D2 selects 48. Off-policy chains: j < 32.
- Chain j at position k uses seed 250000 + 100*j + k and budget META.

For k = 0 to 11:
- one Cache.get batch of the on-policy jobs (memory M_j^(k)), interleaved with the off-policy jobs (memory None); at k = 0 the two policies share one run;
- afterwards, append_once an r_memory record {policy, chain, position, run_key, digest_in, digest_out, n_entries} with identity (policy, chain, position).
After k = 11: an r_chain_done record per chain.

Retention: chains j < 32, seed 265000 + 10*j, budget RETAIN.
- jobshop with memories None, M_j^(3) and M_j^(12);
- quadassign with memories None, M_j^(6) and M_j^(12).
Then the r_retention record, then r_stage_done 'meta'.

6.2 Stage heldout
(1) Preconditions:
- r_stage_done 'meta' must exist.
- H = the categories whose effective role is 'fresh' (expected keys tardiness, quadratic, projects, clique; confirmed at registration).
- Refuse if the ledger holds any run record on them.
- Append the unlock record for role 'fresh' once.
- Build every problem with a dummy Meter (no learner, no score). Drop a category whose fresh problems all carry start_answer, since no capability can change its answers. Wait if fewer than 3 categories remain.

(2) Plan, made before any held-out run:
- U_train(c) and U_test(c) from those problems.
- The registered CPU model c_o0(T) from D4.
- T_c = the largest T in {200, 160, 120, 80, 40} with c_o0(T) <= 60 s.
- Projection = 1.15 x the sum over items of runs x predicted recorded CPU. r0 runs use D4's r0/o0 ratio; matched items count 2 levels; CEIL counts 3.8x.
- H_cap = 300,000 - 1.15 x the recorded CPU of every development and registered run of design r - 15,000.
- Drop items from the end of the priority list until projection <= H_cap. If the primary items alone exceed it, lower T_c of the costliest category by one grid step and recompute.
- Record r_plan.

(3) Priority list. Seeds are 260000 + 10*j + s; c ranges over H; each item is submitted as one interleaved batch.
1. Primary-a: relay and frozen, j < J/2, s < S (S = 2 unless D2 selects 3).
   - Then the futility look (non-binding): t of the J/2 chain means of relay - frozen, recorded as r_futility. If t < 0.5, items 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 are cancelled; items 4, 7, 11 and 12 still run.
   - Then the CPU rule: if sum of relay CPU / sum of frozen CPU exceeds 1.10 on a category over item 1, that category's primary uses frozen@matched = evaluate.raise_until(cache, r0, relay's CPU per (c, seed), budget HELD(c)). The same rule applies to every later r0 arm against relay.
2. Primary-b: relay and frozen, J/2 <= j < J, s < S.
3. shuffled: j < 32, s < 2.
4. o0@matched = evaluate.raise_until(cache, o0, relay's CPU per (c, seed), budget HELD(c)): j < 32, s < 2.
5. offpolicy: j < 32, s < 2.
6. libonly: j < 32, s < 2.
7. frozen@4B (budget CEIL): j < 32, s = 0.
8. prioronly: j < 32, s < 2.
9. depth 8: j < 32, s = 0.
10. depth 4: j < 32, s = 0.
11. References o0@40 and a0@40 (budget REF): j < 16, s = 0.
12. a0@matched: j < 16, s = 0.

Before each item, re-project with the measured CPU per run. If the projection exceeds H_cap, stop and record r_cap. Each matched item gets an r_matched record {arm, keys, reached, levels, budgets}. The stage ends with r_stage_done 'heldout' {arms: run keys}.

6.3 Development modes d1, d2, d4 and dry: scratch ledger, source categories only.

7. relay_report.py
It reads the ledger and writes rsi6/results/relay_report.json. Nothing it computes feeds back into the experiment.

The statistic:
- delta = acquired(A) - acquired(C), paired by (j, c, s).
- The report asserts that untrained(A) == untrained(C) for every r0 arm and for o0: they share programs, constants and the apply stream. The registered min(change of acquired, change of gain) therefore equals the change of acquired. For a0 the report uses min with experiments.report.both_interval.
- Chain mean D_j = the mean over c of the mean over s. Tests are one-sided t-tests on chain means.

Endpoints:
- E-R1 (primary): relay - frozen (frozen@matched where the CPU rule applies), all J chains. Met if t >= t(0.99, J-1); that is 2.387 at J = 64.
- Gate (fixed sequence, family-wise error at most 0.01):
  - only if E-R1 is met: E-R2, relay - shuffled (j < 32, s < 2), at 0.01;
  - only if E-R2 is met: Holm at 0.01 over three endpoints:
    - E-R3: relay - o0@matched. It is void, and so not met, if any pair is unreached or got less CPU than relay (evaluate.compare's rule).
    - E-R4: relay - offpolicy.
    - E-R5: relay - libonly.
  - An arm that was not measured fails its endpoint.

Success tiers:
- T1 = E-R1 and E-R2: the record carries information that helps on these unseen categories.
- T2 = T1 and E-R4 and E-R5: recursive, beyond accumulation and beyond retained macros.
- T3 = T2 and E-R3: useful at matched compute.
'Recursive improvement observed' may be stated only at T3. 'Established' needs replication on an independent set at 0.05.

m_net (registered definition):
- m_net = the minimum, over C in {frozen, shuffled, offpolicy, libonly, o0@matched}, of the mean over chains j < 32 (s < 2) of the chain-mean difference relay - C, in acquired-score units.
- m_net_LB = the minimum over C of (mean_C - t(0.99, 31) x se_C), a Bonferroni-adjusted one-sided 95% bound.
- Also reported: m_net / gain(frozen).

Reported, not tested:
- E-R1 with bootstraps over chains and seeds, and over categories and seeds.
- Per-category signs; negative transfer below -0.005.
- L1: frozen - o0@matched.
- L2: frozen@4B - frozen.
- L3, per arm and category: informative share, d+ per informative variant, switches per program round, share of acquisitions keeping a switched program, share keeping a spliced block.
- L4: the mean Spearman correlation of the per-cell m_c/ubar between pairs of source categories.
- L5: shuffled - frozen.
- L6: Spearman between w(M_j), fixed before any held-out run, and the frozen runs' realized U_c/N_c (cells with N_c >= 5), per category, with w(shuffled) as placebo.
- L7: on-policy minus off-policy at positions 1 to 11 for chains j < 32: d+ per informative variant, switches per round and CPU per switch; reported separately at the category-switch positions 3, 6, 9 and 11.
- L8: the depth curve, M^(4), M^(8) and M^(12) each minus frozen, and its slope.
- The 2x2 decomposition (prior x library).
- Retention: R_JS = acq(M^(12)) - acq(M^(3)) and the within-category benefit acq(M^(3)) - acq(None), both on job shop part B; R_QAP = acq(M^(12)) - acq(M^(6)) on quadratic assignment part B.
- CPU, meter units and constructions per arm.
- The share of runs with acquired at or above the run's threshold.
- The references.

8. REGISTRATION (registration_r.json, written after D0 to D6, reviewed twice, then recorded)
- seed 29.
- generation_0: version digest, and file hashes for every file in 0.1 and 0.2.
- meta: ORDER, J, J_off 32, seeds, budget META; retention chains 0 to 31.
- heldout: role 'fresh', the categories, HELD and the size rule, the D4 coefficients and r0/o0 ratio, seeds, S, the priority list, the pair sets, the futility look, the CPU rules, the cap.
- Endpoints, gate, tiers, m_net, and the predictions with their expected values.
- The development record: D0 to D6 and every decision they triggered.
- Alpha spending: 0.05 in total over all further registered success claims; 0.01 is spent here; each later attempt gets at most 0.01 and is judged on categories no earlier attempt evaluated on.
- what_cannot_be_removed:
  - the training split does not depend on the seed;
  - the instruction set, the sensors, the edit cells and the relay rule are human-written;
  - held-out instance sizes are read at the start of the held-out stage;
  - designs q and r are dispatched at runtime;
  - every arm shares the test-time local improvement.
- reproduction: install() before any run; batching by position; the random streams; ties go to the higher value, then the first proposed; bootstraps of 5,000 draws seeded by the CRC-32 of the comparison's name; a stopped stage replays from the start.
- Seed ranges are disjoint from registration_o's and from development's (600000 and up).

9. TESTS (test_design_r.py)
- T1: empty memory gives design q. LearnerR(r0) and LearnerQ(q0) produce equal capabilities, answers and report counts, on both fixtures, ordered and free, at limits 30, 2,000, 60,000 and 200,000. Foreign entries pass through and change nothing.
- T2: the meter is respected; the same seed and memory give the same record.
- T3: prior_from recovers planted statistics; the cap, kappa, rounding and the dmean rule.
- T4: credit: ties carry no credit; sum(N) equals the number of informative variants; sum(U) = sum(d+); credit is fractional across a variant's edits.
- T5: splice: validity, placeholder remapping, appending of term blocks, base indices kept, size limits, and a round trip from extraction to splice.
- T6: library extraction: liveness, the lib_per_run limit, relocation.
- T7: memory transforms: exactness, and the multisets and block structure that shuffled must preserve; offpolicy assembly; stable digests.
- T8: dispatch: designs.py's sha256 equals registration_o's pin; designs a, b and o give identical results before and after install(); q and r reach their learners.
- T9: no leakage: new entries hold only the listed keys.
- T10: a dry ledger that is stopped and restarted replays and agrees.
- T11: the report on a synthetic ledger rejects E-R1 for a planted +0.01 effect and does not reject under the null.

Machine CPU-seconds, counted as recorded CPU x 1.15:

If the futility look stops the held-out stage, about 88,000 is saved. Wall time after development is about 17.5 hours.

development_checks: D0 (no CPU). Run tests T1 to T11 of test_design_r.py. What would change the design: any failure blocks every later check. In particular, if T1 shows that an empty-memory r0 differs from design q's generation 0, the copy of _acquire_open or _variant is wrong and must be fixed before any CPU is spent.

D1 (about 4,000 machine CPU-s). Categories: job shop, quadratic assignment and p-median. Seeds 600001 to 600006, budget HELD at T 200 (all 24 fresh instances). Arms: r0 with empty memory (= frozen), o0, o0@matched (raise_until to r0's CPU), and r0 at train 800. Measure: program rounds, informative share, switch rate, kept-program share, the r0/o0 CPU ratio, the sd of r0 minus o0, L1_dev and L2_dev (r0@800 minus r0@200). What would change the design: (a) an r0/o0 CPU ratio above 1.25 means adding a behaviour-neutral compile cache, re-running T1, before D2; (b) the measured ratio replaces 1.1 in the held-out plan; (c) L2_dev feeds D2's stop rule.

D2 (about 11,400). Leave one category out (job shop, quadratic assignment, p-median in turn). For each left-out category f, run 8 development chains over the registered ORDER without that category's block and without bin packing (seeds 610000 + 1000f + 100j + k). Then run relay, frozen and shuffled on the left-out category at HELD (seeds 620000 + 1000f + 10j + s, s < 2). Measure: sigma-hat (the within-chain sd of relay minus frozen); tau-hat^2 = max(0, var(chain means) - sigma-hat^2/2); the development effect with its 80% interval; library size; prior concentration; the relay/frozen CPU ratio; informative share by arm; and the prospective Spearman correlation of rule dplus and of rule dmean with the next acquisition's realized per-cell confirmed-switch rate. Pre-written changes: (a) (J, S) becomes the cheapest of (48,2), (64,2), (48,3) with power at least 0.85 at 0.007, using sigma* = max(sigma-hat, 0.025) and tau* = max(tau-hat, 0.008); if none qualifies, use (64,2) and register its MDE. (b) If the median library size is below 2, drop the library: libonly, prioronly and E-R5 are removed, and the Owner's comparison 3 then coincides with frozen. (c) If rho(dmean) - rho(dplus) >= 0.15 and rho(dplus) < 0.10, use rule dmean. (d) If the median prior puts more than 50% of its mass on 3 cells, set beta to 0.5. (e) If L2_dev < 0.003 and the upper 80% bound of the development effect is below 0.003, do not register: record the development negative as an object-level limit and give the budget to a substantively different mechanism. (f) If the relay/frozen CPU ratio exceeds 1.10 on any development category, plan frozen@matched for every held-out category.

D3 (no CPU). Compute L4 (the cross-category Spearman correlation of the per-cell learned statistics) from the D2 chains. What would change the design: it sets the expected value registered for P3. If it is at most 0.1, the registration states that transfer of discovery knowledge is predicted to fail, and lowers P7 and P10 to match.

D4 (at most 1,000). Fit recorded CPU = a + b*train*U_train + d*U_test by OLS on the D1 and D2 runs, per design, and register the residual sd and the r0/o0 ratio. What would change the design: if the projected total at the chosen (J, S), with planning held-out costs, exceeds 300,000 after the priority drops, J falls to the next grid value that keeps power at least 0.8 at 0.007. Otherwise the achieved MDE is registered.

D5 (about 2,000). Dry run: relay.py --dev dry with J 4, J_off 2, positions 0 to 3, budgets divided by 20, and two source categories standing in for the held-out ones. Stop it once and restart it, then run relay_report on the dry ledger. What would change the design: any disagreement on replay, any memory-digest mismatch or any report error blocks registration.

D6 (no CPU). Null calibration of the chain-mean t-test: 20,000 simulated nulls built from centred pair differences resampled from D1's r0 - o0 and from q_compare's q0 - o0, plus chain noise N(0, tau*^2), at the registered J and S. What would change the design: if the rejection rate at t(0.99, J-1) exceeds 0.013, E-R1 to E-R5 switch to a sign-flip permutation test on chain means (10,000 seeded flips) before registration.
what_it_cannot_show: It cannot show that the learner discovers new learning principles. The init, propose and update programs, and the split between representation search and parameter learning, stay fixed. The recursion is one level deep (discovery record to discovery operators), and the rule that updates it is human-written.
Radical novelty. Credit-assigned adaptive operator selection, probability matching and reuse of a block library are known components. What is new is the test and its controls, not the mechanism.

Generalisation beyond these four categories. Inference treats the categories as fixed. An 'established' claim needs replication at 0.05 on an independent set (the sealed targets after their test, or new categories).
Effects below the minimum detectable effect, about 0.005 to 0.007. A negative bounds the effect; it does not show that the effect is zero.

Separate verification of every generation. On held-out categories only memory depths 4, 8 and 12 are measured, at an MDE of about 0.008. Gains that appear only after many more generations are not seen.

Whether a gain arises for the stated reason. Avoiding no-op or destructive variant slots, for example pick edits on ordered problems, is learned information that pays off mechanically. L3's informative share separates part of this, not all of it.

Open-ended capability expansion (the Phase P saturation problem). The instruction set, sensors and edit cells are human-written, and the library only recombines them. Blocks are single-edit fragments; hierarchical composition is not implemented. Nothing outside the construction-policy representation can be acquired.
Retention of capabilities. No capability is carried across categories; only retention of discovery knowledge on two source categories is measured.
A clean causal split between library and prior. The 2x2 decomposition on 256 pairs has an interaction MDE of about 0.0085.

Anything at the registered train 40, or without test-time local improvement. Binary held-out categories may be insensitive to construction policies, as knapsack is (0.9069 for every mechanism), which dilutes the four-category mean.
That the Owner's comparison 3 ('retains skills') is fully represented. It is implemented as retained macros (library-only), not as warm-started programs.
Effects of the chain's order. The order is fixed. Within one category, a chain's three acquisitions see the same training instances relabelled, so the record is narrower than 12 acquisitions suggest.
rejected_and_why: 'statistics' as the base. Its recursion is probably never exercised: R and F share every run until a principle change, and the principle cells screened harmful. Its race and panel re-measure the same part-A instances, because the split does not depend on the seed, so they certify instance-conditional source acceptances. Its fitted mixture rests on duplicated confirmations (2 distinct candidates) and is inconsistent with the -0.0088 screening mean. It drops the randomised discovery controls.

'generator' as the base. Its forecast is analytic and unsimulated. It rests on a single-edit true sd of 0.004 inferred from r = 0.10, which has an SE of about 0.14 and includes duplicates. Additivity of 8-edit macros is untested, and the pass probability ranges from 0.03 to 0.45 as the mean per edit moves by +-0.001. Its G* versus G_R0 comparison is close to automatic. It has no accumulation control. Its E_meta power ignores the category level. Its pooled posterior removes replication.

'level' as the base. Its in-run acceptance is uncalibrated: requiring 4 of 6 wins passes a null candidate with probability 0.34. Its layout is impossible on p-median, which has 10 training instances. Its cross-category recursion rests on two chains (power 0.15 to 0.25). It needs 12 times the budget on categories of unknown cost, and it is close to a repackaging of design q.

'unconventional' as the base. Taking the best of about 1,000 simulated candidates selects surrogate errors, and its D4 gate does not measure fidelity in that upper tail. The independent table of 20 other problems cannot be built for p-median (10 instances) or bin packing (20). It freezes the score and pick programs, which goes against instruction 14. Its only powered recursion test runs inside the simulator.

The decisive proposal's derangement placebo. It is anti-informative: it guarantees that destructive cells receive non-destructive weights. Replaced by a uniform random permutation drawn per chain, which is equally peaked and carries no information in expectation.

The decisive proposal's credit, mean d shrunk toward 0. No-op variants (d = 0, for example pick edits, which always tie on ordered job shop) would outrank every cell with a negative mean and soak up variant slots. Replaced by probability matching on d+ with exact ties excluded; centred mean d is kept as the pre-written alternative.

The decisive proposal's edit to designs.py. registration_o pins that file, and its later stages check the hash. Replaced by a runtime dispatch in a new file, with an identity test for designs a, b and o.
The decisive proposal's 32 x 4 layout. Same held-out cost as 64 x 2, but MDE80 rises from 0.0054 to 0.0064 at tau 0.008, and from 0.0074 to 0.0098 at tau 0.015.

Using budget_scaling's 0.015 to 0.006 as a gain in precision per CPU-second. That figure is the heteroscedastic noise of edit-minus-parent means over eight edits, dominated by p-median, and job shop's sigma rose. Train 200 is kept only because it gives the inner search 5 times more program rounds and because o0 saturates there.
A warm-start 'retains skills' arm that carries kept programs. It changes untrained answers and so needs a second statistic. Library-only is used instead.
A relayed allocation channel (the share of program rounds). It would let the relay win by searching less, which confounds E-R1 with being more like o0.

Design o's discoverer, CEM over cell weights, run inside acquisition as a fourth chain type. With one sample per weight vector it is a less efficient estimator than direct credit assignment, and it does not fit in the day's budget.
Lowering test_e to remove knapsack-type flatness on binary categories. That departs from the registered run budget; the dilution risk is named instead.
Layout-conditional priors. There are too few entries per layout across five source categories. Layout is recorded for diagnostics only.
Tuning beta, kappa or cap on source categories beyond the pre-written alternatives.
Dropping knapsack from the chains. Its fresh scores are flat, but its training-problem statistics are informative, and it is the only binary source layout (two of the held-out categories are binary).
More off-policy chains (64) for the secondaries. That would improve the E-R4 MDE from 0.0088 to 0.0078 for about 16,000 CPU-s and would shrink the reserve below 30,000.
